summary: Enclosed tower in Tuolumne County on the Stanislaus NF; a 1939 sunlight-through-glass fire was spotted from it; a 2011 photo shows the foundation; FFLA lists it gone.

facts.status_note: The FFLA California list and the Forest Lookouts page both mark the tower removed or gone. A 2011 photo shows the foundation.

events.note: Peakbagging photo page says the tower was probably built in 1936; no other information
Lookout-fireman Carpenter on duty at the tower in August 1939
Grass fire started by sunlight focused through a piece of window glass; spotted from the lookout; the item calls it the first such fire in the Stanislaus NF

notes_for_editor: The 1936 build date rests on one Peakbagging photo page ('probably'), with no second source. The 1939 fire account is a reprint of a California Ranger item, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; we did not read the original. Not used: two Calisphere and UC Davis photos titled Thompson Peak Lookout near Janesville and near Susanville, which appear to show the Plumas County site; and a Stanislaus NF Facebook throwback post about 1938 (not readable in the cache), plus a comment there suggesting the tower burned, which is not a source. A reviewer could check the Stanislaus NF post or Forest Service history for a build or removal date.
